solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sprang back and did the twist again?

parts.note: RE- is the prefix meaning once more
to twist something round is to coil it, so did the twist means coiled

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a dance move after attempting the Twist a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did the twist' reads as the 1960s dance, but it just means wound into coils; RE goes in front for 'again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring or jump backwards, as a gun does on firing.

clue.text: Hamlet — as described by 12 — having some verbena dotted around?

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the hidden letters the other way
some of the words verbena dotted holds the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A question about Shakespeare's prince, perhaps surrounded by scattered herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ENAD from verbENA Dotted and 'around' turns it backwards. Hamlet is called 'the gloomy Dane', 12 across giving GLOOMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, a native of that country, famously melancholic.

clue.text: Shame about Green Berets' outerwear — it's a mess!

indicators.note: about means the word for shame goes round the other letters

parts.note: a shame, as in 'what a shame', is a pity

indicators.note: outerwear is the outside layer, so only the first and last letters of Green Berets are used

explanation.surface: Pity the special forces soldiers whose uniforms are filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outerwear' takes the outside letters G and S of 'Green Berets', which go inside PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty is a byword for a filthy, untidy room, so it serves as an example of a mess.

clue.text: Caper — not cold — put into pudding is capital

indicators.note: put into means the trimmed word goes inside the pudding

parts.note: sago is a milk pudding made from palm starch

indicators.note: not means the letter for cold is taken away

parts.note: a caper is a playful prank or antic
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction: a caper goes into a warm pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops C (cold) from ANTIC to leave ANTI; 'put into' places it in SAGO. 'Caper' looks like the pickled bud of cookery but is a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: Resident bowler in grudge match?

parts.note: a local is someone living in the area
a derby is the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A home-town cricket bowler takes part in a bitter contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket but is the hat, called a derby in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A local derby is a game between neighbouring rivals, typically fought with extra feeling, hence a grudge match; the question mark admits it is an example.

clue.text: Beat back expert supporting divinity

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the word for expert goes underneath

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject of divinity
a buff is an enthusiast who knows a lot about something

explanation.surface: An expert theologian backs up religion and drives off an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supporting' puts BUFF below RE, religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff is to repel or reject an approach, driving it back.

clue.text: Scary pieces in performance having no end of effect

parts.note: chess pieces are called men

indicators.note: having no signals that a letter is removed from the word for performance

parts.note: acting is a stage performance

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of effect

explanation.surface: Chess pieces in a show that lacks a scary finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' are chessmen, not fragments; 'having no' with 'end of' drops the T that closes 'effect' from the performance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing means threatening, which is frightening or scary.

clue.text: Ignoring following, fobbing off historian

indicators.note: off means the remaining letters are disordered
ignoring means the letter for following is left out

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone brushing aside a historian while ignoring what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring' drops F from FOBBING to leave OBBING; 'off' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon wrote The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Flier's overcoat misplaced or untraceable

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the bird to its wordplay

indicators.note: misplaced means the remaining letters are put in a new order
untraceable means the word or cannot be found among the letters, so it is dropped

explanation.surface: A pilot's lost overcoat cannot be tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untraceable' removes O and R from OVERCOAT, leaving VECOAT, which 'misplaced' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill, and so a flier.

clue.text: Group of rescue volunteers held back powerful emotion

indicators.note: held back means those letters are read the other way
group of means a cluster of letters is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lifeboat crew restrained their strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of' takes EVOL from rescuE VOLunteers; 'held back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the archetypal strong feeling, an example of a powerful emotion.

clue.text: Rub at smuts spoiling foundation

indicators.note: spoiling means the letters of the preceding words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbing at soot marks ruins someone's make-up base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundation' looks like cosmetics, the smuts ruining it, but means an underlying layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A substratum is an underlying layer on which something rests, a base.

clue.text: Shadowy overhang built in to gallery's wings

indicators.note: built in to means the word for overhang goes inside
wings are the two sides, so the outer letters of gallery are taken

parts.note: to loom is to hang over something menacingly

explanation.surface: A dark ledge is built into the sides of an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' gives G and Y, the ends of 'gallery', and LOOM is 'built in to' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy means dark and full of shade, which is shadowy.

clue.text: Where in Paris I dig difficult road for panel conveying messages

parts.note: où is French for where
a dig is a poke or jab

indicators.note: difficult means the letters of road are put into a tricky order

explanation.surface: Asking a Parisian where to dig up an awkward road for a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: OU is French for 'where'; 'difficult' rearranges ROAD to OARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ouija board is a lettered board used at seances to spell out supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Working together with officer periodically

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
and means together with
OFF is the abbreviation for officer

explanation.surface: Someone working alongside an officer only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: On and off means intermittently, at intervals, which is periodically.

clue.text: International in twenty-four hours? Piece of cake!

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for twenty-four hours

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: An international match won in a day was easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' suggests something easy, but a dainty is a small delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty is a small, delicate cake or sweet, so a piece of cake literally.

clue.text: Plant, originally treating aluminium recyclables, recently accepted glass or nickel

indicators.note: originally means the start of each word is taken

parts.words: treating aluminium recyclables, recently accepted glass or nickel

explanation.surface: A recycling plant that has just begun taking aluminium, glass and nickel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a recycling works, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic herb, a plant used in cooking.

clue.text: They say starter perhaps is lacking in taste

indicators.note: they say means we hear a word spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a starter is one course of a meal

explanation.surface: Diners say the first course of the meal is bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in taste' suggests bland food but means vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or vulgar, without refinement or good taste.

clue.text: Coming out from questionable interest group, carelessly store away …

indicators.note: questionable means the letters of interest group are suspect and reordered
carelessly means the letters of store are taken out in no particular order
away means those letters go from the larger set

explanation.surface: A dodgy lobby group sloppily stashing something before it bursts out.
explanation.walkthrough: From INTEREST GROUP take the letters of STORE, which are scattered; what is left, INTEGRUP, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that is erupting has lava bursting or coming out of it.

clue.text: … announcements about American university's grants

indicators.note: about means the announcements go round the university

parts.note: ads are advertisements, announcements
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is an American university; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Adverts about an American university's funding awards.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 18 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to concede or allow it, so the verb grants fits.

clue.text: Created a dry pub? That's not allowed!

definitions.meaning: read as ..., a pub with its bar removed, so no drink

explanation.surface: Someone protests that turning a pub teetotal breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Debarred means barred or excluded, prohibited from doing something.

clue.text: Compositions for training Sue and Ted to play

indicators.note: to play means the letters of the two names are moved about

explanation.surface: Practice pieces written for two young musicians to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Etudes are musical pieces written as exercises to develop technique, studies for training.

clue.text: Happy the solver's participating in joke, up to a point

indicators.note: participating in means the word for the solver goes inside
up to a point means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: to josh is to joke or tease
the solver is you, the person reading; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: The solver is pleased to share in a joke, within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the solver' is the reader, a familiar crossword device; 'up to a point' drops the joke word's last letter and 'participating in' sets the reader inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyous means full of joy, which is happy.

clue.text: 'One Prophesying Destiny' appearing in miscellany

parts.note: Job is honoured as a prophet in Islam
one's lot is one's destiny or fate

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's title appears in a mixed collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is a mixed assortment of items sold together, a miscellany.

clue.text: Wing-walking alone?

parts.note: a wing-walker stands on a plane's wing, so pictured literally as ..., with the idea of isolation from 'alone'

explanation.surface: A daredevil performs stunts on an aircraft wing with nobody else.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in an exposed, isolated position without support, as a lone wing-walker is.

clue.text: Husband swallowed powerful emotion

parts.note: something swallowed has been eaten, so ate

explanation.surface: A husband gulps down a strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate is intense dislike, an example of a powerful emotion.

clue.text: Amused expression from ambassador — on helium!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: An ambassador giggles after inhaling helium.
explanation.definitionFit: He-he is a written representation of a giggle or chuckle.

clue.text: Fence of stakes to provide odd fish

parts.note: a weir can be a fence of stakes set in a river to trap fish
to do a meal is to provide it

explanation.surface: A staked fence built in a stream to supply strange fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd fish' looks like a catch from the weir, but is slang for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd fish is an eccentric person, which is exactly what a weirdo is.

clue.text: Composing number including middle section in old style

indicators.note: including means the song goes round the other letters

parts.note: a number is a song in a show

indicators.note: middle section in means only the inner part of the style's name is kept

parts.note: Gothic is an old style of architecture and lettering

explanation.surface: Writing a song in an old-fashioned style, with a middle eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle section in' strips G and C from GOTHIC to give OTHI, which SONG is 'including'. 'Composing' is not writing music but calming.
explanation.definitionFit: Composing as in calming, the way one composes oneself, is what something soothing does.
